title: EdgeFusion operator compatibility & quantization pilot sync
summary: Redwood and EdgeFusion reviewed operator compatibility for marketplace listing and an initial quantization pilot. Discussed K8s operator changes, KMS/HSM integration, networking egress, performance expectations and a small benchmark plan. Agreed on pilot scope, who will run the first of three experiments, and next steps to get security docs and marketplace packaging checklist shared.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-08-30
Start: 14:00 PDT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Samira Khan (Redwood AE), Diego Morales (Redwood SE), Priya Patel (Redwood), Markus Li (EdgeFusion CTO), Hannah Ortiz (Platform Eng), Ravi Desai (Security Architect)

--- Auto-generated summary (may be imperfect) ---
We went through operator compatibility items, clarified what EdgeFusion needs for marketplace listing (onprem operator + helm chart + marketplace manifest), and sketched a 3-experiment quantization pilot (baseline float32 -> int8 -> 4-bit q + perf). Security questions on KMS/HSM, audit logs and SSO were raised. Action items assigned and timeline agreed.

00:00 Speaker 1 (Samira): ok hi everyone thanks for hopping on, um this is Samira from Redwood, i'm the AE on this account, Diego will do the deep parts, and Priya's on for packaging questions.
00:28 Speaker 2 (Markus): hey thanks, Markus here, sorry i was late getting off another call, we have hannah and ravi with me. want to get clarity on what we need to change to our k8s operator to be marketplace-ready.
00:55 Speaker 1 (Samira): great, quick agenda: operator compatibility matrix, quantization pilot scope, security (kms/soc2), networking/egress for listing, and next steps. sound good?
01:12 Speaker 3 (Diego): yeah i can jump in on operator changes — main things we usually look for are: helm chart linting, images in partner registry or an approved repo, an operator that can be configured to point to redwood runtime endpoints, and a lightweight smoke-test that marketplace runs. also, if you want to support private (VPC) deployments there are extra flags for endpoint discovery and certs.
01:45 Speaker 4 (Hannah): ok on helm chart linting, our operator already has a helm wrapper but the current manifests assume an internal loadbalancer — is that a blocker?
02:05 Speaker 3 (Diego): not necessarily, but marketplace verification expects both clusterIP and loadbalancer deployment patterns documented. we can help with a small overlay. also please try to avoid hard-coded egress IPs; we prefer dns-based endpoints so customers can route to redwood regions or your onprem control plane.
02:40 Speaker 2 (Markus): got it, we can add overlays. question on images: do you want the operator image in your partner registry or can we provide via our artifact repo?
03:05 Speaker 1 (Samira): partner registry is preferred for the listing flow — easier for marketplace test harness. but we can accept signed images from your repo if you provide an SBOM and signature.
03:30 Speaker 5 (Ravi): quick security question: for the private deployment where keys are customer-managed, how do you integrate KMS/HSM and what level of audit logs do you keep?
03:52 Speaker 3 (Diego): good q. we support KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and bring-your-own HSM via KMIP). for marketplace listing we need a short integration guide showing key rotation, envelope encryption, and what logs are forwarded — redwood keeps per-request audit traces for control-plane ops but we replay only markers, we don't retain raw payloads by default. we'll share the SOC2 summary.
04:30 Speaker 1 (Samira): note to attendees: i'll put the SOC2 and the KMS integration guide in the shared drive after the call.
04:45 Speaker 4 (Hannah): thanks. on quantization pilot, we want to understand throughput gains without hurting user-facing quality. what's typical?
05:05 Speaker 3 (Diego): typical improvements vary by model and prompt length — for some LLMs int8 gives ~1.7-2.3x token throughput improvement, 4-bit (q4) can be 2.5-3x but with quality tradeoffs. we recommend a three-step pilot: baseline float32, int8, and a low-bit run, and measure latency P50/P95, token cost, and a small human eval set.
05:40 Speaker 2 (Markus): that's helpful. can we scope a short benchmark harness? we have 5k daily active users, peak QPS ~18, and long-form prompts like 800 tokens sometimes.
06:05 Speaker 3 (Diego): perfect, that's the kind of data we need. for 800 token prompts, batching behavior and KV cache changes matter — we'll share a recommended batch size and kv-cache configuration to keep latencies within your SLO.
06:40 Speaker 1 (Samira): Priya, any notes on packaging and marketplace metadata?
06:50 Speaker 6 (Priya): yes, marketplace wants clear references: listing blurb, tested K8s versions (1.26+ ideally), operator CRD definitions, required RBAC, sample helm values for private VPC mode, and an automated smoke test. also a small listing image (1280x720) and a concise checklist. i'll draft a template.
07:20 Speaker 4 (Hannah): CRD and RBAC is a bit manual for us today; happy to follow your template. on RBAC, do you require pod identity / IRSA patterns?
07:40 Speaker 3 (Diego): not strictly, but we recommend using pod-level service accounts with minimal permissions, and for AWS we prefer IRSA. we'll document recommended policies.
08:10 Speaker 5 (Ravi): on compliance: what about data residency? if a customer requires EU-only residency, can the operator ensure traffic stays in region and not sent to hosted endpoints?
08:35 Speaker 3 (Diego): yes — you can pin the runtime endpoints to a region by setting the endpoint URL in the operator config. for complete air-gapped, we have an on-prem package but that typically moves to a private deployment contract. for marketplace listing it's fine to say both hosted and private options exist.
09:05 Speaker 2 (Markus): ok can you outline the pilot timeline? we'd like to run this in september.
09:20 Speaker 1 (Samira): we proposed a three-week pilot cadence: week 0: prep and image deploy, week 1: baseline run float32 + SLO capture, week 2: int8 tests + regression eval, week 3: low-bit exploratory and decision. we can compress if you want.
09:48 Speaker 4 (Hannah): september timeline works. one ask: can you share recommended prompt sets for human eval?
10:00 Speaker 3 (Diego): we have a small starter prompt set and a human eval rubric — i'll share a spreadsheet link. it's not perfect but it's a good starting point for quality delta comparisons.
10:20 Speaker 6 (Priya): also we'll need to know what telemetry hooks the marketplace runner uses — traces, token counts, latency metrics, error codes — so you can map them to your dashboards.
10:40 Speaker 3 (Diego): we'll publish a telemetry spec: per-request token count, latency P50/P95, model variant, quantization flag, and an error taxonomy.
11:00 Speaker 5 (Ravi): about encryption in flight and at rest — is TLS mutual required for private deployments?
11:20 Speaker 3 (Diego): mutual TLS is optional but recommended for private. for hosted API we use mTLS between control-plane components, and customers use TLS for data in transit. for on-prem we can require mTLS and bring-your-own certs.
11:45 Speaker 2 (Markus): networking egress — marketplace tends to run tests from a central account; do we need to whitelist IPs?
12:05 Speaker 1 (Samira): marketplace test harness prefers no fixed IPs. that's why we prefer DNS endpoints and peering options. if you need IP whitelisting we can provide a set but it's less flexible.
12:30 Speaker 4 (Hannah): noted. any thoughts on throttling and autoscaling behavior for the operator? we expect bursts during product launches.
13:00 Speaker 3 (Diego): autoscaling recommendations: horizontal pod autoscaler with CPU+custom metrics (inflight requests), GPU autoscaler for model servers. we have autoscaler hooks in the operator that can signal desired scale based on queue depth. also suggest a small warm pool for cold starts.
13:35 Speaker 2 (Markus): warm pool — would that increase cost significantly?
13:48 Speaker 3 (Diego): it depends — warm pools keep some capacity idle, so cost is higher but P95 latency improves. we can run a cost/latency tradeoff simulation during the pilot.
14:05 Speaker 6 (Priya): ok switching to packaging edge-case: signature and SBOM — marketplace wants SPDX or CycloneDX, do you accept either?
14:20 Speaker 3 (Diego): either is fine, we prefer CycloneDX but SPDX acceptable. signed images + attestation are recommended.
14:40 Speaker 5 (Ravi): regulatory question: for customers in finance with strict logs retention, can we configure the operator to drop verbatim request content and only keep meta-audit entries?
15:00 Speaker 3 (Diego): yes — operator logging level can be set to redact payloads. we'll include exact flags in the operator manifest.
15:20 Speaker 1 (Samira): quick note — i'll attach a sample operator values file that has these logging flags toggled.
15:30 Speaker 2 (Markus): good. uh any competitor callouts? we compared this with DynServe and NimbusAI — curious what makes redwood different in terms of runtime optimizations.
15:50 Speaker 3 (Diego): two things: our runtime does continuous batching with kv-cache awareness and kernel selection tuned per sequence-length distribution; second is smart routing for fallbacks to cheaper variants. both reduce unit cost and give predictable latency.
16:20 Speaker 4 (Hannah): can you give an example of kernel selection affecting latency?
16:30 Speaker 3 (Diego): sure — for short contexts we switch to a kernel path that reduces per-token overhead; for long form we prefer a different attention kernel that's memory efficient. effects can be 10–40% depending on model.
16:55 Speaker 5 (Ravi): back to KMS: does redwood store any customer key material?
17:05 Speaker 3 (Diego): no — in BYOK modes, keys stay in customer KMS/HSM; we hold only envelope key metadata. we'll provide the KMS integration doc.
17:25 Speaker 1 (Samira): ok let's walk through the pilot acceptance criteria — Markus, what would you call success?
17:40 Speaker 2 (Markus): baseline P95 under 1.2s for our most common prompt, int8 should keep P95 within 1.5x baseline and cost per token less than 60% of baseline. quality delta < 5% on our rubric.
18:10 Speaker 3 (Diego): reasonable. we'll try to hit those targets. if int8 fails quality we can try q4f (mixed quant) or mixed precision splicer.
18:30 Speaker 6 (Priya): packaging question — are there required labels for the marketplace? like semantic versioning and publisher ID?
18:45 Speaker 1 (Samira): yes, include semver, publisher name, partner ID (we'll provide), and a short release notes file for the listing.
19:00 Speaker 4 (Hannah): were there any constraints on operator CRDs that would break our existing controller?
19:15 Speaker 3 (Diego): only two things: avoid embedding endpoint secrets in CRD spec (use external secret or KMS reference), and emit status conditions for model-ready and health. other than that, CRDs are fine.
19:40 Speaker 2 (Markus): good. about the smoke test you mentioned earlier, what does it look like?
19:55 Speaker 3 (Diego): typically: deploy operator+helm values, create a sample CR that spins up a small model server, run 50 scripted requests (mix of short and long), verify latency < threshold and tokens/response match expected, and validate RBAC doesn't allow cluster-admin access.
20:25 Speaker 6 (Priya): we'll wire that into our CI to run on PRs if possible.
20:40 Speaker 5 (Ravi): let's talk about billing and metering requirements for the marketplace listing — do you need token-level metering exported?
21:00 Speaker 1 (Samira): marketplace wants token counts and model variant per request; for dedicated/paying customers we'll export billing hooks to your billing endpoint or you can pull usage via our API.
21:20 Speaker 4 (Hannah): ok thanks. switching gears slightly: if we list both hosted and onprem, how do you represent the offering in the marketplace? one tile, two options?
21:35 Speaker 1 (Samira): usually one listing with toggles: hosted, dedicated, private; the listing metadata clarifies what's included in each. Priya will include a sample manifest that reflects multi-mode offerings.
21:55 Speaker 2 (Markus): all right, shall we set dates for the pilot?
22:05 Speaker 1 (Samira): propose start week of 2027-09-06. that gives you a week to get images and manifests ready. does that work?
22:18 Speaker 2 (Markus): yep september 6 works.
22:25 Speaker 3 (Diego): i'll prepare a benchmark harness and test image. note: for long prompts we'll simulate streaming generation to emulate your client behavior.
22:45 Speaker 4 (Hannah): what about monitoring — do we need to install a sidecar or use your telemetry endpoint?
23:00 Speaker 3 (Diego): sidecar optional; operator emits prometheus metrics and we can provide a small Grafana dashboard template. for critical traces we send spans via OTLP if you enable it.
23:20 Speaker 5 (Ravi): security again — SSO and RBAC for the console: do you support SAML and SCIM for provisioning?
23:35 Speaker 1 (Samira): yes SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning are supported for console. for operator-level RBAC we rely on k8s service accounts. we'll share the SSO integration guide.
24:00 Speaker 6 (Priya): sharing links now: i've dropped three docs in the chat — packaging checklist (link), sample values file (link), and the initial operator manifest (link).
24:20 Speaker 2 (Markus): got them thanks.
24:30 Speaker 3 (Diego): one more nuance: quantization profiles need different kernel paths, so operator should allow selecting runtime variant per model. otherwise you'll end up with brittle config toggles.
24:55 Speaker 4 (Hannah): noted. is that runtime variant selection per CR?
25:05 Speaker 3 (Diego): yes per model CR it's cleaner.
25:20 Speaker 1 (Samira): ok big-picture: deliverables before pilot: marketplace checklist (Samira), operator test image (Diego), sample prompt set + eval rubric (Diego), SOC2/KMS docs (Samira), EdgeFusion provides perf targets and sample traffic (Markus).
25:50 Speaker 2 (Markus): confirmed. any blockers on your side?
26:00 Speaker 1 (Samira): none immediate. small ask: can you provide a sample cluster (k8s version + cloud) where we'll run initial smoke?
26:12 Speaker 2 (Markus): yes we'll carve out a dev cluster on EKS 1.26 for the test.
26:25 Speaker 5 (Ravi): one last compliance nuance — some customers require attestations for SBOMs. do you accept signed attestations?
26:40 Speaker 3 (Diego): yes signed attestations are acceptable, and we can accept in-toto attestation.
26:55 Speaker 6 (Priya): i put a preliminary checklist item to add attestations.
27:05 Speaker 4 (Hannah): for the pilot, who runs the human eval? us or redwood?
27:20 Speaker 3 (Diego): ideally we run the automated tests and you run the human eval for product acceptance. we can help with setup and provide the rubric.
27:40 Speaker 2 (Markus): fine. how long do you need to configure kv-cache for our long-form use case?
27:55 Speaker 3 (Diego): kv-cache tuning is quick — a day of initial test to pick window sizes; the pilot will refine it.
28:10 Speaker 4 (Hannah): about logs again — can we route audit logs to our SIEM?
28:25 Speaker 3 (Diego): yes, operator can forward to your SIEM via syslog/OTLP; we'll provide examples.
28:40 Speaker 5 (Ravi): great. any final risk areas we should flag?
28:50 Speaker 1 (Samira): two risks: quantization quality regressions (we'll flag via evals) and network egress constraints in some enterprise customers (we'll mitigate via peering or private deployment).
29:10 Speaker 2 (Markus): good to know. can you outline rollback steps if a quantized run shows bad regression?
29:25 Speaker 3 (Diego): operator supports versioned model CRs and automatic fallback to baseline variant; we also have traffic-splitting so you can canary new variants.
29:45 Speaker 4 (Hannah): ok perfect.
30:00 Speaker 6 (Priya): i'll summarize packaging items in the checklist and share after the call.
30:10 Speaker 1 (Samira): before we wrap — any open questions?
30:18 Speaker 2 (Markus): one: do you have any latency guarantees for dedicated capacity?
30:28 Speaker 3 (Diego): with Dedicated we provide SLO-backed latency targets (we can share example SLA text). it's part of a dedicated contract.
30:40 Speaker 5 (Ravi): and on data retention, will redwood delete logs on request?
30:50 Speaker 3 (Diego): yes we support data deletion requests and can provide deletion attestations for specific tenants.
31:05 Speaker 2 (Markus): good. last minor thing — will your marketplace listing show cost estimates per million tokens?
31:20 Speaker 1 (Samira): yes, we'll show unit economics and a cost estimator in the listing page.
31:35 Speaker 4 (Hannah): that helps.
31:45 Speaker 6 (Priya): ok i'll create the draft listing copy and circulate.
31:55 Speaker 2 (Markus): all right, looks like we're aligned. thanks everyone.
32:05 Speaker 1 (Samira): quick recap of next steps and owners (see action items). i will attach SOC2 + KMS guide, priya will send checklist, diego will publish test image and harness. we start pilot week of 2027-09-06.
32:30 Speaker 3 (Diego): i'll also put the benchmark harness in the partner repo and tag it.
32:40 Speaker 5 (Ravi): thanks, looking forward.
32:50 Speaker 2 (Markus): thanks all.
33:00 Speaker 1 (Samira): meeting adjourned.

--- End transcript ---
